title: Keep repository READMEs approachable and separate from change histories
abstract: Write a repository README as a professional, welcoming orientation for new visitors: briefly explain what the project is, its value, how to get started, and links to relevant resources. Do not use it as an accumulating changelog, internal progress log, or dump of implementation details. Put extensive explanations, designs, technical references, and long-form guides under docs/; where a chronological change history is useful, maintain a separate changelog file such as CHANGELOG.md and link to it. Brief release highlights in a README are permissible when helpful.

source.reference: Generalized README presentation and documentation organization preference; no private conversation retained

scope_hints.scope_boundary: Repository README files intended for a public or prospective contributor audience; README summary and navigation are allowed, lengthy docs belong under docs/, and a separate changelog is appropriate when a project tracks substantive history. Do not invent release history or require a changelog in projects that do not need one.

remarks: Normalized and published as NOM-0136; no rule application or unrelated repository action.
